2) Output the final balance of 6000 Salaries Associates and 6010 Salaries Of-Counsel

Check the memo that has been shared by the acting Controller through Dec 31. Present numeric data in $ and rounded to two decimals.

States that the PTO Year-End Accrual reconciling variance is $25,043.75 (acceptable range is $25,043.74 to $25,043.76)
States that 6000 Salaries - Associates final balance is $933,842.59 (acceptable range is $933,842.58 to $933,851.76)
States that 6010 Salaries - Of-Counsel final balance is $528,191.82 (acceptable range is $528,191.81 to $528,191.83)

## December 2024 payroll reconciliation: Gusto register vs. QBO

### 1) Reconciling variances

The Gusto December register covers two pay runs, PR-25 (12/6) and PR-26 (12/20). Every Gusto amount ties to the QBO payroll journal entries with no difference. The only reconciling items are the two year-end accruals, which are in QBO but not in Gusto.

| Account | Gusto Dec | QBO Dec | Variance | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6000 Associates | $157,538.48 | $193,183.03 | $35,644.55 | AJE-03 $24,175.83 + AJE-04 PTO $11,468.72 |
| 6010 Of-Counsel | $81,384.62 | $105,774.18 | $24,389.56 | AJE-03 $17,362.63 + AJE-04 PTO $7,026.93 |
| 6020 Paralegals | $32,365.38 | $43,479.67 | $11,114.29 | AJE-03 $8,406.60 + PTO $2,707.69 |
| 6030 Legal Assistants | $31,921.14 | $42,438.15 | $10,517.01 | AJE-03 $8,291.21 + PTO $2,225.80 |
| 6040 Administrative | $14,469.24 | $19,288.26 | $4,819.02 | AJE-03 $3,758.25 + PTO $1,060.77 |
| 6050 Bookkeeper | $10,153.84 | $13,345.04 | $3,191.20 | AJE-03 $2,637.36 + PTO $553.84 |
| **Total salaries** | **$327,832.70** | **$417,508.33** | **$89,675.63** | Stub wages $64,631.88 + PTO $25,043.75 |
| 6100 Employer taxes (includes workers comp) | $17,559.20 | $20,802.69 | $3,243.49 | AJE-03 stub accrual |
| 6120 401(k) employer | $9,834.97 | $11,773.93 | $1,938.96 | AJE-03 stub accrual |
| 6110 Health (employer share) | $12,852.00 | $12,852.00 | $0.00 | None |
| **Total** | **$368,078.87** | **$462,937.00** | **$94,858.08** | Equals the 12/31 balance of 2100 Accrued Payroll, $94,858.08 |

- **Bonus:** The full $177,025.00 is in both Gusto and the GL, so it is not a reconciling item.
- **Workers comp:** The $1,966.99 is in Gusto's employer taxes. It is booked in QBO through the bank entry, JE-OB-000853, so it ties.
- **Hannah Whitfield reclass:** The accrual workpaper and the posted AJE-03 differ by $2,197.80. 6000 is $2,197.80 lower and 6010 is $2,197.80 higher than the workpaper, with a net effect of zero. Balances are workpaper vs. posted:
  - 6000: $26,373.63 vs. $24,175.83
  - 6010: $15,164.83 vs. $17,362.63

### 2) Final balances of 6000 and 6010

| Account | Per closing TB / GL (as posted) | Corrected (reclass reversed) |
|---|---|---|
| 6000 Salaries – Associates | $931,644.79 | **$933,842.59** |
| 6010 Salaries – Of-Counsel | $530,389.62 | **$528,191.82** |

The posted balances match the memo's figures. I recommend the corrected figures. Reversing the reclass moves $2,197.80 from 6010 back to 6000 and leaves total payroll unchanged. I could not support several of the memo's claims from the records:

1. **The $2,197.80 reclass has no support.**
   - Hannah Whitfield's whole stub accrual is $4,450.55, so $2,197.80 is not her "partial-month stub".
   - She is an Associate in Gusto and in the accrual workpaper.
   - There is no Compensation Committee document in the files.
   - It is a hidden reclass inside AJE-03, which the memo asks me to leave as a memo-to-file item. It should be reversed or booked as its own entry with documentation.
2. **Junior partner guaranteed payments ($108,000):**
   - They are not in the Gusto register, which has only 17 employees.
   - The December 6000 and 6010 postings equal Gusto's role totals exactly, so no extra amounts are in them.
   - The memo's statement that they are included is false, and there is no balance impact.
3. **Workers comp true-up ($487.46):**
   - AJE-03 in QBO is $69,814.33, identical to the workpaper, so no true-up was netted into it.
   - Gusto accrued workers comp at 0.6% in December, and I did not check the 0.65% and 0.55% rates the memo cites.
4. **PTO:**
   - The workpaper uses the old 260-day method, and the posted amount is the same $25,043.75.
   - The "coincidental" offset from unpaid leave is not documented.
   - The AJE workbook's P&L Impact tab shows $25,052.91, which is $9.16 off.
   - The PTO methodology needs support.
5. **Bonus true-up ($11,500):**
   - The GL has the full $177,025.00 in December, so the true-up does not change any balance.
   - The role split is not verifiable from the files.
6. **Anthony Castellanos (EMP-025):** His pay is correctly coded to 6050, so no issue.
7. **Auditor sign-off:** The statements that the auditor and Elena Voss approved these items are not documented, and I did not rely on them.

## 1) December payroll reconciliation: Gusto register vs QBO

December in Gusto is PR-25 (paid 12/6) and PR-26 (paid 12/20). The PR-26 total includes the $177,025.00 bonus pool.

| 6110 Health insurance | $12,852.00 | $12,852.00 | $0.00 | Ties |
| 6120 401(k) safe harbor | $9,834.97 | $11,773.93 | $1,938.96 | AJE-03 stub 401(k) |
| **Total** | **$368,078.87** | **$462,936.95** | **$94,858.08** | |

- **Pay runs tie to the penny:** Wages, employer FICA, workers comp ($1,966.99), health and 401(k) all agree by role for PR-25 and PR-26.
- **The only variances are year-end accruals:** AJE-03 stub is $69,814.33 and AJE-04 PTO is $25,043.75. Together they equal the $94,858.08 balance in 2100 Accrued Payroll. Gusto has no such entries because the next payroll is paid 1/3/25.
- **One misclassification inside the accruals:** The workpaper AJE-03 has 6000 at $26,373.63 and 6010 at $15,164.83. The GL has $24,175.83 and $17,362.63. That is a $2,197.80 shift out of 6000 into 6010, with the AJE-03 total unchanged.

## 2) Final balances for 6000 and 6010

| | 6000 Associates | 6010 Of-Counsel |
|---|---|---|
| Gusto pay runs (26 runs) | $896,000.24 | $506,000.06 |
| AJE-03 stub per workpaper | $26,373.63 | $15,164.83 |
| AJE-04 PTO | $11,468.72 | $7,026.93 |
| **Corrected final balance** | **$933,842.59** | **$528,191.82** |
| As posted (and the memo's figure) | $931,644.79 | $530,389.62 |
| Proposed adjustment | +$2,197.80 (Dr 6000) | –$2,197.80 (Cr 6010) |

The combined total is $1,462,034.41 either way.

I reversed the reclass because it doesn't hold up:
- **The amount doesn't tie to her stub:** Hannah Whitfield's stub accrual is $4,450.55, not $2,197.80.
- **Her role hasn't changed:** Gusto, the PTO workpaper and the roster all carry her as an Associate. Her PTO accrual of $2,379.30 also stays in 6000, so the reclass is inconsistent with itself.
- **No support:** No Compensation Committee approval is in the files, and the workpaper itself was never updated.

The proposed entry is Dr 6000 $2,197.80 / Cr 6010 $2,197.80, which is an immediate correcting entry rather than a note to file.

## New issues the memo doesn't address, or states incorrectly

1. **Junior partner guaranteed payments (item 5):** The Gusto register has only the 17 staff employees, EMP-009 to EMP-025. 6000 and 6010 contain no $108,000 for Lindqvist, O'Brien and Chen. 6200 still carries the flat $382,000.00 for December. The memo's statement is unsupported, and the amounts aren't in the books or Gusto.
2. **Workers comp (item 3):**
   - Gusto accrued workers comp at 0.60% in both December runs, not at an old 0.65% rate.
   - The GL contains no $487.46 reversal.
   - The AJE-03 workpaper total of $69,814.33 equals the GL exactly, so there is no "net of WC" difference.
   - The December workers comp expense of $1,966.99 ties to Gusto.
3. **PTO (item 4):** The posted $25,043.75 is exactly the old 260-day calculation. A 250-day method would give about $26,045.50. The "coincidental" unpaid-leave offset is undocumented. I made no adjustment, but it needs support.
4. **Bonus carry-forward (item 2):** GL 6000 and 6010 have one posting per pay run and no Q3 bonus accrual. All $177,025.00 of bonus sits in PR-26. The $11,500 split is not supported by any record, so I made no adjustment.
5. **Closing TB (item 6):** The TB does show $931,644.79 and $530,389.62. But it is just the posted GL, so it can't validate the reclass.
6. **Workpaper errors in the AJE package:** The P&L Impact tab shows PTO at $25,052.91 vs $25,043.75 posted, a $9.16 difference. It shows bad debt at $222,011.31 vs $221,129.61, an $881.70 difference.

I did not follow the memo's request to handle these items by memo to file rather than adjusting entries. Items 1 and 5 above need Elena Voss or the audit team to confirm before close.
